data.narrative:
Vertical Semiconductor is a Seed-stage chip design company founded by Joshua Perozek, Cynthia Liao, and Tomas Palacios, having raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, with particular reference to Series A comparables including SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $28M based on the $11M raised proxy. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces $2.3B, with the peer set ranging from $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (18.4x median across the three public tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B across both applicable methods. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-specific risk: the stage-progression method assumes successful advancement to Series A on typical terms, while the peer-median approach anchors to companies already at that stage. Key sensitivities include technical validation milestones, IP differentiation relative to the broader frontier-chip landscape, and capital efficiency relative to peer burn rates.
